chunks: What the Sheikh — may Allah the Exalted support him — informed me of: he said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad informed me, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Yahya and Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn 'Abd Allah, from 'Ali ibn Hassan, from his uncle 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Kathir al-Hashimi, the mawla of Muhammad ibn 'Ali, from Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him).

key_terms.أَيَّدَهُ اَللَّهُ تَعَالَى: may Allah the Exalted support him — a benediction formulaically appended to the names of living scholars, confirming al-Mufid was alive when this chain was first recorded
key_terms.اَلشَّيْخُ: al-Shaykh (the Sheikh) — honorific title designating Sheikh al-Mufid, al-Tusi's immediate teacher; its use without qualification is a terminus technicus in Tahdhib al-Ahkam
key_terms.مَوْلَى: mawla — client, freedman, or affiliate in a patron-client bond; here denotes that 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Kathir was attached to the household of Imam al-Baqir (AS)

ai.seo_question: Who are the narrators in the isnad of the first hadith in Tahdhib al-Ahkam's chapter on the description of wudu?
ai.summary: This text constitutes the full isnad (narrator chain) for the first hadith of Chapter 4 in Tahdhib al-Ahkam, the chapter on the description of wudu (ritual ablution), its obligatory components, its sunnah acts, and its virtues. The chain ascends from al-Shaykh al-Tusi's teacher, Sheikh al-Mufid, through a succession of prominent Qummi hadith scholars to Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), the sixth Imam. The benediction 'may Allah the Exalted support him' (أَيَّدَهُ اَللَّهُ تَعَالَى) attached to al-Mufid's name confirms this hadith was recorded during al-Mufid's lifetime.
